merger_description:
AVC Operations Pty Limited (**AVC**) proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets of the licensed hotel business trading as Central Hotel in Beaconsfield, Victoria (**Central Hotel**), including the exclusive right to carry on the business in succession of the vendor, and the benefit of the lease, from Beaconsfield Tavern (Operations) Pty Ltd as trustee for Oliver Hume Beaconsfield Tavern Operations Trust  (**Vendor**), under an Asset Sale Agreement (the **Acquisition**).  

  

AVC is a subsidiary of Australian Venue Co. Holdings Limited which operates over 200 licensed venues throughout Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars, clubs and licensed restaurants, and hotel/motels with accommodation services. AVC’s venues are individually branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metropolitan areas, offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and gaming facilities.  

  

Central Hotel is a licensed hotel and associated bottle shop located at 1 Old Princes Highway, Beaconsfield VIC 3807. It is a typical Australian pub/hotel with a bistro space, sports bar, and alfresco dining space.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between AVC and the Central
Hotel in the supply of dining, functions, on-premises liquor
services and off-premises packaged liquor in the local area
surrounding the Central Hotel
b. there are alternative venues that supply dining, functions, on-
premises liquor services and off-premises packaged liquor in
the local area surrounding the Central Hotel.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
